title: Kullu shawl weaving
summary: Kullu shawls are woven from soft wool on a handloom in the Kullu valley of Himachal Pradesh. The body is plain and warm, and each end carries bands of bright geometric pattern called pattis, in reds, greens and yellows against natural white. Patterned shawls became common in the valley after weavers from the neighbouring Bushahr region settled there in the 1940s.
howToPlay: Pick a wool colour and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square of the border to weave that shape there; it is mirrored into the other three corners.
Copy the bands shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The border is mirrored left to right and top to bottom, so each shape you place is repeated on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its wool colour both match the pattern you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: The wool of sheep, and in places of yak or pashmina goats, is spun and woven in the cool valleys of the Himalaya into shawls that keep out cold. A Kullu shawl is recognised by its bands of stepped geometric shapes, which weavers can combine in many ways.
